explore_lenses.label: What did Fauci’s Fifth Amendment claim do?
explore_lenses.title: It halted testimony, not the inquiry
explore_lenses.summary: Fauci appeared pursuant to a subpoena but declined senators’ questions after invoking the privilege against self-incrimination. The assertion protects against compelled potentially incriminating testimony; it does not itself resolve the accusations debated at the hearing.

claims.text: The Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee listed Fauci as the sole witness for its July 29, 2026 hearing, and AP reported that he had been subpoenaed by Chairman Rand Paul.

The Fifth Amendment privilege is available in congressional investigations and, when properly invoked, protects a witness from being compelled to provide statements that could directly or indirectly furnish evidence for a later criminal prosecution.
Whether a particular question is covered can turn on whether answering presents a reasonable risk of incrimination; the privilege is not a ruling that the witness committed wrongdoing.

explore_lenses.label: What are Paul and Fauci actually arguing?
explore_lenses.title: They dispute both conduct and motive
explore_lenses.summary: Paul frames the hearing as an effort to uncover conflicts, withheld information, and possible links between U.S.-funded research and the pandemic. Fauci says Paul’s pursuit of prosecution is the reason he could not safely provide further testimony, while scientists supporting Fauci say the charges lack credible evidence.

claims.text: Paul has argued that officials, advisers, and researchers involved in COVID-19-origin assessments had undisclosed conflicts and that the public and Congress received a curated account; these are the chairman’s allegations, not findings established by the committee page.
Fauci said Paul’s calls for prosecution appeared intended to induce a statement that could put him 'behind bars,' and said he invoked the Fifth Amendment on his lawyers’ advice.

AP reported that more than 150 infectious-disease experts and other scientists publicly defended Fauci, saying no credible evidence supported the charges against him; AP also reported that a 2024 GOP-led House subcommittee found no evidence linking Fauci to wrongdoing.

The dispute over 'gain-of-function' research partly reflects competing definitions: NIH’s prior framework focused on research expected to create, transfer, or use enhanced potential pandemic pathogens, rather than every experiment described broadly as gain-of-function.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next procedurally and on policy?
explore_lenses.title: The subpoena dispute may continue; oversight is already changing
explore_lenses.summary: A valid Fifth Amendment assertion limits Congress’s ability to compel answers, so any effort to force testimony would have to address the privilege’s scope. Separately, federal policy on high-risk biological research has been revised since the pandemic, regardless of what this hearing produces.

claims.text: Constitution Annotated states that a witness who properly invokes the Fifth Amendment in a congressional investigation cannot be compelled to provide potentially incriminating statements or punished for refusing those committee questions.

As a procedural precedent, the Senate HELP Committee in 2024 approved both a proposed civil subpoena-enforcement resolution and a proposed criminal-contempt certification after a witness refused to appear; comparable steps would require affirmative committee and Senate action rather than occurring automatically.

In May 2025, Executive Order 14292 directed agencies to end specified federal funding for dangerous gain-of-function research in countries of concern or without adequate oversight, revise the federal framework, and create public reporting mechanisms for covered research.

Forecast: Any near-term continuation of the dispute is more likely to center on document releases, the scope of the privilege, or a committee enforcement decision than on substantive testimony from Fauci, unless he later elects to answer or receives immunity.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: The Iran War refers to the 2026 international armed conflict centered on Iran, the United States and Israel, with effects extending across the Persian Gulf and neighboring states. U.S. combat operations began on February 28, 2026; the conflict has also made security and commercial navigation in the Strait of Hormuz a central issue.

facts.label: Start date
facts.value: The United States notified the UN Security Council that it commenced combat operations against Iran on February 28, 2026; U.S. energy officials likewise identify military action on that date as the point after which Hormuz traffic was effectively disrupted.

facts.label: Principal parties and stated U.S. purpos
facts.value: In its UN notification, the United States said it was acting in cooperation with Israel, citing protection of U.S. forces and regional partners and the free flow of maritime commerce through the Strait of Hormuz. These are the U.S. government's stated objectives, not an independent legal finding.

facts.label: Legal position asserted by the United St
facts.value: The United States characterized its operations as necessary and proportionate self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter, including collective self-defense of Israel.

facts.label: Why the Strait of Hormuz matters
facts.value: The strait lies between Iran and Oman and links the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea. In the first half of 2025, about 20.9 million barrels per day of oil—roughly one-fifth of global petroleum-liquids consumption—moved through it, while alternative routes could replace only part of disrupted flows.

event_overview.title: About Japan Earthquake
event_overview.subject: Japan Earthquake
event_overview.summary: A magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck the Kumamoto area of Kyushu, southwestern Japan, on July 28, 2026, causing fatalities, injuries and structural damage. The disaster response includes searches for people affected by collapses and monitoring of continued seismic activity, while authorities assess localized tsunami risk and issue public warnings as needed.

facts.label: Date and location
facts.value: The main earthquake occurred on July 28, 2026, in the Kumamoto area of Kyushu, Japan’s southwestern main island.

facts.label: Magnitude and impacts
facts.value: Initial reporting described the earthquake as magnitude 7.1, with destructive shaking that damaged buildings and infrastructure and led to casualties.

facts.label: Earthquake and tsunami authority
facts.value: Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) is the national authority that rapidly determines an earthquake’s location, magnitude and observed intensity, and distributes earthquake information to disaster-prevention authorities and the public.

facts.label: Tsunami alerts
facts.value: When a quake may produce damaging coastal waves, JMA issues tsunami warnings or advisories by forecast region, generally within about two to three minutes; advisories call for people to leave the water and coast until they are lifted.

facts.label: Seismic-intensity system
facts.value: Japan reports local shaking separately from magnitude using JMA’s 10-level seismic-intensity scale, which reflects ground motion at a particular place and can vary with distance and local geology.

event_overview.scope_note: This timeline follows the July 28–29, 2026 Kumamoto-area earthquake, including rescue operations, aftershocks and tsunami alerts; it does not attempt to cover all earthquakes in Japan or every subsequent damage assessment and emergency update.

event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: The Iran War refers to the 2026 international armed conflict centered on Iran, the United States and Israel, with effects extending across the Persian Gulf and neighboring states. U.S. combat operations began on February 28, 2026; the conflict has also made security and commercial navigation in the Strait of Hormuz a central issue.

facts.label: Start date
facts.value: The United States notified the UN Security Council that it commenced combat operations against Iran on February 28, 2026; U.S. energy officials likewise identify military action on that date as the point after which Hormuz traffic was effectively disrupted.

facts.label: Principal parties and stated U.S. purpos
facts.value: In its UN notification, the United States said it was acting in cooperation with Israel, citing protection of U.S. forces and regional partners and the free flow of maritime commerce through the Strait of Hormuz. These are the U.S. government's stated objectives, not an independent legal finding.

facts.label: Legal position asserted by the United St
facts.value: The United States characterized its operations as necessary and proportionate self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter, including collective self-defense of Israel.

facts.label: Why the Strait of Hormuz matters
facts.value: The strait lies between Iran and Oman and links the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea. In the first half of 2025, about 20.9 million barrels per day of oil—roughly one-fifth of global petroleum-liquids consumption—moved through it, while alternative routes could replace only part of disrupted flows.

event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: The Iran War refers to the 2026 international armed conflict centered on Iran, the United States and Israel, with effects extending across the Persian Gulf and neighboring states. U.S. combat operations began on February 28, 2026; the conflict has also made security and commercial navigation in the Strait of Hormuz a central issue.

facts.label: Start date
facts.value: The United States notified the UN Security Council that it commenced combat operations against Iran on February 28, 2026; U.S. energy officials likewise identify military action on that date as the point after which Hormuz traffic was effectively disrupted.

facts.label: Principal parties and stated U.S. purpos
facts.value: In its UN notification, the United States said it was acting in cooperation with Israel, citing protection of U.S. forces and regional partners and the free flow of maritime commerce through the Strait of Hormuz. These are the U.S. government's stated objectives, not an independent legal finding.

facts.label: Legal position asserted by the United St
facts.value: The United States characterized its operations as necessary and proportionate self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter, including collective self-defense of Israel.

facts.label: Why the Strait of Hormuz matters
facts.value: The strait lies between Iran and Oman and links the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea. In the first half of 2025, about 20.9 million barrels per day of oil—roughly one-fifth of global petroleum-liquids consumption—moved through it, while alternative routes could replace only part of disrupted flows.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: The Iran War refers to the 2026 international armed conflict centered on Iran, the United States and Israel, with effects extending across the Persian Gulf and neighboring states. U.S. combat operations began on February 28, 2026; the conflict has also made security and commercial navigation in the Strait of Hormuz a central issue.

facts.label: Start date
facts.value: The United States notified the UN Security Council that it commenced combat operations against Iran on February 28, 2026; U.S. energy officials likewise identify military action on that date as the point after which Hormuz traffic was effectively disrupted.

facts.label: Principal parties and stated U.S. purpos
facts.value: In its UN notification, the United States said it was acting in cooperation with Israel, citing protection of U.S. forces and regional partners and the free flow of maritime commerce through the Strait of Hormuz. These are the U.S. government's stated objectives, not an independent legal finding.

facts.label: Legal position asserted by the United St
facts.value: The United States characterized its operations as necessary and proportionate self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter, including collective self-defense of Israel.

facts.label: Why the Strait of Hormuz matters
facts.value: The strait lies between Iran and Oman and links the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea. In the first half of 2025, about 20.9 million barrels per day of oil—roughly one-fifth of global petroleum-liquids consumption—moved through it, while alternative routes could replace only part of disrupted flows.

event_overview.title: About Ukraine Conflict
event_overview.subject: Ukraine Conflict
event_overview.summary: The Ukraine conflict is an armed conflict that began with Russia’s 2014 seizure of Crimea and fighting in eastern Ukraine, then expanded into a full-scale Russian armed attack across Ukraine on 24 February 2022. It includes frontline combat, long-range missile and drone strikes, attacks affecting civilian infrastructure, displacement, and international legal and diplomatic efforts to end the war and establish accountability.

facts.label: Conflict timeline
facts.value: The UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine has operated since 2014; it identifies 24 February 2022 as the start of the Russian Federation’s full-scale armed attack, after which it focused on the international armed conflict’s human-rights impact.

facts.label: Geographic scope
facts.value: The war affects territory across Ukraine, including areas near the frontline, cities far from it, and territory occupied by the Russian Federation; Kyiv is among the urban centres affected by long-range attacks.

facts.label: Civilian-harm pattern
facts.value: UN monitors reported that long-range weapons, including missiles and drones, were the leading cause of civilian casualties in June 2026, with many casualties occurring in urban areas far from the frontline; short-range drones were a major danger in frontline areas.

facts.label: International position
facts.value: On 2 March 2022, the UN General Assembly adopted resolution ES-11/1, deploring Russia’s aggression against Ukraine and demanding that Russia end its use of force and withdraw its military forces.

facts.label: International Court of Justice proceedin
facts.value: In provisional measures ordered on 16 March 2022 in Ukraine v. Russian Federation, the International Court of Justice directed Russia to suspend the military operations it commenced on 24 February 2022, while stating that the order did not decide jurisdiction or the merits of the case.
